A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to calculate the imaginary part of the static potential in a hot medium, and how to use this result to compute the in-medium quarkonium spectral function.
the thermal width of quarkonium is the same in all channels, and is given by the imaginary part of the static potential.

we have provided a complete, systematic, and fully gauge invariant framework to study quarkonium in a thermal medium in the context of perturbative QCD, which can be used to calculate the in-medium spectral functions of the heavy quarkonia in any channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quarkonium spectral functions in the various channels are all qualitatively similar, in that they are all dominated by a single resonance, with a width that is comparable to the binding energy.
the imaginary part in the static potential, and the ensuing quarkonium disappearance, is a generic feature of any hot QCD medium, irrespective of whether it is in a quark-gluon plasma phase or not.
the imaginary part in the heavy quark potential, which has a simple perturbative form, is the dominant contribution to quarkonium dissociation in the plasma.
